features.name: Reproducible JDK 21 baseline selection
features.behavior: The standard startup path node harness/init.mjs discovers and selects an installed JDK 21 before running Maven verification, so the baseline goes green from a clean checkout without a manual JAVA_HOME export
features.falsifier: The startup path still inherits the host default Temurin 25 and the Maven Enforcer [21,22) rejects it, goes green only because JAVA_HOME was pre-set to a manually selected OpenJDK 21, or passes by relaxing the Enforcer range or dropping the runtime-version assertion [X-004]

context.note: Make the Maven branch of harness/init.mjs select an installed JDK 21 (set JAVA_HOME and PATH only for the spawned ./mvnw) before verification, so a clean checkout greens with no manual export. The host default /usr/bin/java is Temurin 25.0.3; Homebrew OpenJDK 21 lives at /opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@21/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home but is keg-only (/usr/libexec/java_home -v 21 returns temurin-25), and env/local.json's java.executable=/usr/bin/java is stale. Keep the pom.xml Enforcer [21,22) and BaselineTest's Runtime.version().feature()==21 intact as the independent discriminator.

evidence.result: exit 1: Maven Enforcer rejected Temurin 25.0.3 — 'Detected JDK version 25.0.3 ... is not in the allowed range [21,22)'
exit 0: './mvnw -q verify' passed under the selected Homebrew OpenJDK 21 (BaselineTest Runtime.version().feature()==21 green)

features.checkerNotes:
APPROVE: env -u JAVA_HOME node harness/init.mjs reproduces green (exit 0) with no manual JAVA_HOME export; host Temurin 25 goes red (exit 1) under the untouched Enforcer [21,22) and BaselineTest feature()==21, so the green is a genuine JDK-21 selection, not a relaxed discriminator or a pre-set JAVA_HOME. Baseline now auto-selects Homebrew OpenJDK 21 for the Maven branch; `env -u JAVA_HOME node harness/init.mjs` is green (exit 0) after a recorded red (exit 1, Enforcer rejected Temurin 25).

harness/init.mjs: discoverJdk21Home() checks the keg-only Homebrew keg (/opt/homebrew/opt and /usr/local/opt) and verifies its release file says JAVA_VERSION=21, then sets JAVA_HOME and prepends its bin to PATH only for the spawned ./mvnw; if no JDK 21 is found it inherits the environment so the Enforcer still reports the truthful red. harness/env/local.json: java.home and java.executable now point at the Homebrew OpenJDK 21 keg. Enforcer [21,22) and BaselineTest's Runtime.version().feature()==21 are untouched.

checkerVerdict.reproduction: env -u JAVA_HOME node harness/init.mjs -> exit 0 (Baseline green); control env -u JAVA_HOME ./mvnw -q verify -> exit 1 (Enforcer: Detected JDK version 25.0.3 not in [21,22))
checkerVerdict.observed: discoverJdk21Home() returns /opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@21 (release JAVA_VERSION=21.0.12.1) and sets JAVA_HOME/PATH only for the spawned ./mvnw; pom.xml Enforcer [21,22) and BaselineTest Runtime.version().feature()==21 untouched; fallback (no JDK 21 -> inherit env -> Enforcer red) honest.
checkerVerdict.exitCriterion: Satisfied: env -u JAVA_HOME node harness/init.mjs exits 0 from a clean checkout with no manual JAVA_HOME export, and the discriminator is real (Temurin 25 -> exit 1).

runs.result: Maven Enforcer rejected Temurin 25.0.3: 'Detected JDK version 25.0.3 ... is not in the allowed range [21,22)'.
Baseline green — './mvnw -q verify' passed under the selected Homebrew OpenJDK 21 (JAVA_HOME/PATH set for the spawned ./mvnw only).

adversarialChecks.cleanup: not-applicable: the fix creates no files, ports, or long-lived processes — JAVA_HOME/PATH are scoped to the short-lived ./mvnw subprocess
adversarialChecks.concurrency: not-applicable: single-threaded baseline gate; no shared state or parallelism introduced
adversarialChecks.discrimination: Any wrong selection — inheriting the host Temurin 25, or using java_home -v 21 which also returns Temurin 25 — turns the recorded env -u JAVA_HOME run red rather than green, and the untouched Enforcer [21,22) plus BaselineTest feature()==21 independently reject a non-21 JVM; the only anchor the runs do not independently pin is the release-file version check, which is redundant on success here because the keg genuinely holds 21.

residualUnknowns: The absent-JDK-21 fallback (discoverJdk21Home() returns null -> inherit env -> Enforcer red) was verified by code path and the recorded pre-fix red run, not by removing the keg (non-destructive constraint).
The Intel-Homebrew (/usr/local/opt) and Windows (mvnw.cmd) discovery paths are candidates but untested on this Apple Silicon machine.

features.name: Sanitized normalized ingestion
features.behavior: IngestService.ingest(String) parses one serialized v1 JSON object, returns the stable accepted or rejection result, and invokes IndexPort exactly once only with a sanitized normalized document for an eligible valid record
features.falsifier: The service bypasses the serialized ingress seam, accepts an out-of-scope, incomplete, or unsupported-major record, invokes IndexPort for a rejection or other than exactly once for an acceptance, or exposes a configured secret or additive-field overwrite in the indexed document [INV-SCOPE-1] [INV-REDACT-1] [INV-META-1] [INV-SCHEMA-1]

context.note: First map service/src/main/java as Maven's main sourceDirectory in pom.xml, then implement the complete approved public seam in the ingest package: ingest(String) -> IngestResult over a supplied IndexPort, NormalizedLogRecord, and the typed bounded LogQuery family required by IndexPort.search. Validate scope and required wire fields, normalize, redact, then make the single index call; use the five stable rejection codes and the context packet rather than exposing parser helpers. The package-scoped path is deliberate because Java requires ten mutually dependent public contract types in separate source files and a partial IndexPort would be a temporary incompatible API.

evidence.result: Tests run: 2, failures: 2, errors: 0; both assertions report the required public IngestService contract absent.
Tests run: 2, failures: 0, errors: 0; acceptance sanitizes and indexes exactly once, and five invalid partitions never index.
Independent black-box oracle passed all 5 scope, redaction, metadata, additive-v1, and unsupported-major conditions.

features.checkerNotes: APPROVE: `./mvnw -q -Dtest=IngestServiceTest test` reproduces green (exit 0; Tests run: 2, Failures: 0, Errors: 0). Black-box reflection asserts sanitized/redacted exactly-once indexing and the five rejection partitions against hardcoded literals, so the test is neither tautological nor written-from-code and discriminates a wrong implementation.

checkerVerdict.exitCriterion: Satisfied: acceptance indexes exactly once with redaction; the five invalid partitions never index.

runs.result: 5 independent black-box contract tests passed under OpenJDK 21.

adversarialChecks.cleanup: not-applicable: ingest owns no external resource or returned lifecycle handle
adversarialChecks.concurrency: not-applicable: ingest keeps immutable policy/port references and no mutable per-request state
adversarialChecks.discrimination: The ingest runs do not exercise every constructor invariant in the typed query family, so an incorrect query-limit validator could survive until the storage-adapter feature exercises it.

residualUnknowns: Typed query execution semantics remain owned by the later OpenSearch adapter feature.

checkerVerdict.exitCriterion: Satisfied: scope, redaction, metadata, additive-v1, and unsupported-major conditions all enforced before indexing.

runs.result: 5 black-box contract tests passed under OpenJDK 21.

adversarialChecks.cleanup: not-applicable: the capturing index port and service allocate no external resources

features.name: Bounded read-only MCP service
features.behavior: The authenticated Streamable HTTP MCP service exposes only search_logs and get_failure_context and enforces correlation, 15-minute, 200-record, 256-KiB, five-second, and no-pagination limits
features.falsifier: A tool falls back from a supplied run id, accepts an unbounded request, exceeds a budget, writes the index, or invokes Kubernetes [INV-CORR-1] [INV-BOUND-1] [INV-READ-1] [X-006] [X-007]

context.note: Use supplied test.run_id exclusively; otherwise require namespace, workload, and interval, then cap before reading.

features.name: MCP wire and authorization contract
features.behavior: A Streamable HTTP contract proves ServiceAccount JWT authorization, the exact two-tool surface, bounded truncation metadata, validation errors, and absence of write or Kubernetes capabilities
features.falsifier: Direct tests pass while a missing or invalid JWT reaches tool dispatch or index query, a valid JWT is denied before normal validation, initialization exposes non-tool capabilities, the tool list contains anything beyond search_logs and get_failure_context, an unknown tool reaches the index, or a pagination, response-size, or deadline bound is violated [INV-AUTH-1] [INV-TOOLS-1] [INV-BOUND-1] [INV-READ-1]

context.note: Start the real loopback HTTP boundary only through McpServiceBootstrap.start(McpHttpServerConfig(port 0), capturing IndexPort, deterministic ServiceAccountJwtValidator), drive endpoint() as an MCP client, and always close RunningMcpServer; observe authorization, closed tool surface, budgets, and side effects only through wire responses and captured dependencies.
